name: Dennewitz
summary: Ney, sent in Oudinot's place to take Berlin, marched across the front of the Army of the North towards Jüterbog. Bertrand's corps ran into Tauentzien's Landwehr at Dennewitz, which held through the morning until Bülow's corps came in on the French flank at midday. Reynier's Saxons took Göhlsdorf and held it, but as Borstell arrived on their flank about four, Ney ordered Oudinot's corps across the rear of the battle to his other wing; the Saxons were left alone and broke, the French line went with them, and Ney's army streamed back on Torgau, losing some 20,000 men. The Saxons and Bavarians took their defeat as a sign to change sides.

forces.name: Morand's Division
forces.summary: Bertrand's leading division, which came on Tauentzien's corps across the Agerbach at Dennewitz in the morning and fought the Prussian Landwehr there until Bülow's brigades came up on its flank.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
The 13th and 23rd Line's regimental artillery companies are from Nafziger's IV Corps return of 20 September, each shown as a section of regimental guns.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Fontanelli's Division
forces.summary: Bertrand's Italians, who came up beside Morand against Tauentzien's line and were drawn into the fighting round Dennewitz and Rohrbeck as Bülow's corps arrived.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Italian list, the nearest to 1813.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
The Milan Guard Battalion, a city guard and not the Royal Guard, is shown as Line.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Franquemont's Division
forces.summary: The Württemberg contingent, with Jett's chevau-légers, on Bertrand's left. It fought for Göhlsdorf and Rohrbeck against Bülow's brigades through the afternoon and lost heavily in the rout; after the battle it was down to four combined battalions.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Württemberg 1812 list, the nearest to 1813.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
The foot battery, four 6-pdrs and two howitzers, is the list's Light Artillery.
Jett's two regiments had about 300 men between them a fortnight later.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Dombrowski's Division
forces.summary: The Polish division of Bertrand's corps, two infantry regiments and Krukowiecki's light horse, which covered the corps' flank and fell back with it.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Grand Duchy of Warsaw list, the nearest to 1813.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
Nafziger has the 2nd Polish attached to Durutte's division; it is shown here with its own division, as the French list can't take it.
One infantry brigade for its cavalry brigade, where the list wants two, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Sahr's Division
forces.summary: Reynier's leading Saxon division, which took Göhlsdorf in the afternoon and held it against Bülow's attacks until Borstell's brigade came up on its flank about four; when Oudinot's corps was moved away behind it, the Saxons were left alone, and broke.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Saxon 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: the Saxon army that fought in 1813 was rebuilt from the survivors of Russia on the same lines.

After Nafziger's order of battle for Großbeeren, a fortnight before: his Dennewitz return gives the Saxons as one division, an organisation he notes was only set up on 17 September, so the two divisions of August are kept here.
Each brigade's foot battery, with fewer than the six battalions the list wants for it, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Le Coq's Division
forces.summary: Reynier's second Saxon division, fed into the fight for Göhlsdorf beside Sahr's and carried away in the rout when the line broke behind it.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Saxon 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: the Saxon army that fought in 1813 was rebuilt from the survivors of Russia on the same lines.

After Nafziger's order of battle for Großbeeren, a fortnight before: his Dennewitz return gives the Saxons as one division, an organisation he notes was only set up on 17 September, so the two divisions of August are kept here.
Le Coq is the book's named commander.
The battalion of the Guard Grenadiers is shown as Grenadiers.
Each brigade's foot battery, with fewer than the six battalions the list wants for it, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Generalleutnant Le Coq (Saxon Corps), with his own rating.

forces.name: Gablenz's Light Cavalry
forces.summary: Reynier's Saxon horse, the Hussars and the Prinz Clemens Uhlans, which tried to cover the corps' retreat after Göhlsdorf.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Saxon 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: the Saxon army that fought in 1813 was rebuilt from the survivors of Russia on the same lines.

After Nafziger's order of battle for Großbeeren, a fortnight before: his Dennewitz return gives the Saxons as one division, an organisation he notes was only set up on 17 September, so the two divisions of August are kept here.
The Hussars had eight squadrons, so they are Large; the Uhlans had five.
The brigade was led by Oberst von Lindenau for Gablenz, who commanded the corps cavalry.
Cavalry without infantry shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Durutte's Division
forces.summary: The French division of Reynier's corps, in support of the Saxons at Göhlsdorf, caught up again in their rout.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
Its battalions were mostly young conscripts of the classes of 1813 and 1814. They are rated as ordinary Line, as they fought: the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit those who broke more readily.
Its battalions were well under strength after Großbeeren; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit many of them.
Two light regiments, where the list allows one in a division, and two Würzburg battalions as Rheinbund infantry, where it allows one, show as historical departures.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Raglovich's Division
forces.summary: Oudinot's Bavarian division, single battalions of many regiments and two Jäger battalions, which marched off with the rest of the corps at Ney's order and covered the retreat.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1813, still on the French side.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
Its line battalions were each from a different regiment; they are grouped in pairs as the brigades' regiments, as the list takes them.
Nafziger doesn't say what the two foot batteries were; one is shown as the list's Light Artillery, the other as Foot Artillery.

forces.name: Beaumont's Cavalry
forces.summary: Oudinot's corps cavalry, three regiments of German light horse.

After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
The Hessian and Bavarian Chevau-légers are shown as Westphalian Hussars, the list's other light cavalry.
Three regiments, where the list's brigade takes two, and a cavalry brigade with no infantry brigade to allow it, show as historical departures.

forces.name: Arrighi's Cavalry
forces.summary: The army's cavalry reserve, squadrons from many regiments, which covered the retreat after the French line broke.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.

Most regiments sent one or two squadrons, so each listed regiment is shown as a unit; the dragoon brigades' many single squadrons are paired, two regiments to a unit, and the 13th Cuirassiers' one squadron rides with the 27th Dragoons.
Ameil's three hussar regiments, where the list's brigade takes two, show as a historical departure. The corps' other horse batteries, more than the list takes, are on the Not in this force card.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Tauentzien's Corps
forces.formation: IV Corps, Army of the North
forces.summary: Almost all Landwehr, standing across the road to Jüterbog, it took Bertrand's attack in the morning and held on at Dennewitz for hours against odds until Bülow's corps came in on the French flank.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
Nafziger gives the corps' infantry as Lindenau's one division; it is split into the two brigades of his Großbeeren return, Dobschütz's and Lindenau's.

A reserve regiment of three musketeer battalions, Landwehr regiments of four battalions, Lindenau's brigade with no line regiment, and six Landwehr cavalry regiments in one brigade, where it takes five, show as historical departures.
The half horse battery #6 rides with the Landwehr cavalry.

Batteries beyond the one each brigade takes are in the corps artillery, as the list's reserve takes them; more than it allows, or a reserve horse battery with fewer brigades than the list wants for it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: Ilovaisky #3 Don Cossacks
missing.reason: A Russian Cossack regiment with the corps, which a force from the Prussian list can't take.

forces.name: Bülow's Corps
forces.formation: III Corps, Army of the North
forces.summary: Marching to Tauentzien's help, Thümen's and Hesse-Homburg's brigades came in on Bertrand's flank at midday and Krafft's soon after; Borstell, ordered elsewhere, came on his own initiative about four and struck the Saxons at Göhlsdorf. With Oudinot's corps marched away behind them, the French line broke.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.

Nafziger lists the 1st Leib Hussars with both Thümen and Hesse-Homburg; they are shown once, with Hesse-Homburg, as at Großbeeren. The Brandenburg Dragoons, attached to Thümen, and the West Prussian Dragoons, to Krafft, are a dragoon brigade of their own.

Each brigade's grenadier battalion is with its first line regiment. Line and reserve regiments of three or more musketeer battalions, Thümen's brigade with no Landwehr and three line regiments, Landwehr regiments of four, two attached hussar regiments where the list allows one, line and Landwehr cavalry brigades together, and two 12-pdr batteries where the corps artillery takes one show as historical departures.
Thümen's 12-pdr battery and Krafft's two 12-pdr howitzers are in the corps artillery.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Pahlen's Advance Guard
forces.summary: The head of Winzingerode's Russian corps, which reached the field about six as the French gave way, and joined the pursuit.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Dennewitz.
A Jäger brigade of one regiment, and cavalry with no infantry brigade to allow it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 1 of the 2 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.
